Below is a quick recipe you can drop straight into your shell (inside the **Documentation** folder) to pull the very first line of *ArchivedFinalReport2024.txt*, break it into individual words, sort those words alphabetically, and print the tidy sentence back to the console.

> ⚠️ **Tip:** All the utilities used below – `awk`, `tr`, `sort`, `paste` – come pre‑installed on almost every Unix‑like system. They work fine with plain‑text files regardless of their extensions.

---

### One‑liner

```sh
awk 'NR==1{print;exit}' ArchivedFinalReport2024.txt \
    | tr '[:space:]' '\n'   # put each word on its own line
    | sort                   # alphabetical ordering
    | paste -sd ' '          # glue the sorted words back together
```

#### What happens step‑by‑step?

| Stage | Command fragment | Purpose |
|-------|------------------|---------|
| **Get the first line** | `awk 'NR==1{print;exit}' ...` | Prints only record 1 (the first line), then stops processing further input. |
| **Split into words** | `tr '[:space:]' '\n'` | Replaces every space/tab/newline with a newline so each word becomes a separate line. |
| **Sort alphabetically** | `sort` | Orders those single‑word lines lexicographically. |
| **Reassemble** | `paste -sd ' '` | Joins the sorted list back into one line, separating words again with spaces. |

The resulting output will look something like:

```
Alpha Beta Gamma Delta Epsilon Zeta ...
```

with all the words from the opening line arranged in strict alphabetical order.

---

### Optional: Save the cleaned line to a new temporary file

If you prefer to keep the reordered line somewhere handy, simply redirect the output:

```sh
awk 'NR==1{print;exit}' ArchivedFinalReport2024.txt \
    | tr '[:space:]' '\n' | sort | paste -sd ' ' > SortedFirstLine.tmp
```

Now `SortedFirstLine.tmp` contains exactly that neat, alphabetized sentence.

Feel free to tweak the separator (`-d ' '` in `paste`) if you want commas, tabs, or anything else between the words. Happy sorting!
